findings.title: Stored XSS in the Projects table lets any workspace writer execute script in other members' browsers.
findings.attacker: Any authenticated workspace member with write access to projects (owner, admin, or member).
findings.input: Project fields persisted in the `projects` table, including `name`, `type`, `description`, `dueDate`, and client-linked display data.
findings.attack_path: The attacker enters a JavaScript payload into a project field through the project modal. `persistProjectToSupabase()` stores those raw values in the org-scoped `projects` table, other members load that data through `fetchProjectsFromSupabase()`, and `renderProjects()` injects the fields directly into `tbody.innerHTML` without escaping, executing the payload in the victim browser.
findings.impact: A malicious workspace member can run arbitrary JavaScript in another member's authenticated session, use `window.supabaseClient` or the victim's live page context to read or mutate workspace data, invoke authenticated edge functions, and effectively act as the victim inside the app.
evidence: `src/legacy/financial-core.js` reads raw project form values and saves them into the in-memory project object in the project modal handler.

`src/legacy/financial-core.js` -> `projectRowForDb()` copies `name`, `type`, `description`, and related fields straight into the database payload; `persistProjectToSupabase()` upserts that payload to `projects`.
`src/legacy/financial-core.js` -> `fetchProjectsFromSupabase()` selects all project rows for the current organization and maps them back into UI objects.
`src/legacy/financial-core.js` -> `renderProjects()` concatenates `p.name`, `clientName`, `p.type`, `p.description`, and `p.dueDate` straight into `tbody.innerHTML` with no `esc()` call.
`src/legacy/supabase-auth.js` exposes the live authenticated Supabase client as `window.supabaseClient`, which injected script can use once it gains execution.

findings.title: Stored XSS in custom project status labels executes when teammates open the status manager.
findings.attacker: Any authenticated workspace member with write access to workspace app settings (owner, admin, or member).
findings.input: A custom project status label entered through the Projects status-management UI and stored in org-scoped `app_settings.project_statuses`.
findings.attack_path: The attacker adds a malicious status label through the Manage statuses flow. `persistAppSettingsToSupabase()` saves `project_statuses` into the shared org `app_settings` row, other members load those labels during workspace hydration, and `renderStatusList()` inserts each label directly into `statusList.innerHTML` without escaping when the status manager is opened.
findings.impact: Opening the status manager is enough to trigger arbitrary JavaScript in the victim browser, enabling the attacker to hijack or use the victim's authenticated in-app session and perform actions as that user.
evidence: `src/legacy/financial-core.js` lets users add arbitrary status labels through the `btn-status-add` handler and immediately persists them.
`src/legacy/financial-core.js` -> `persistAppSettingsToSupabase()` writes `project_statuses` to the shared org `app_settings` row.
`src/legacy/financial-core.js` loads `settingsRow.project_statuses` during workspace hydration and stores them into `projectStatuses` for later rendering.
`src/legacy/financial-core.js` -> `renderStatusList()` concatenates each raw `label` into `statusList.innerHTML` with no escaping.
`supabase/migrations/20260301107000_organizations_multitenancy.sql` gives authenticated org writers update access to `app_settings`, so an ordinary member can plant the payload for other members.
